acceptanceCriteria: The domain accepts optional standard or express priority, rejects invalid priority, records positive backorder shortages, keeps the order cancellable, and lists backorders.
The application service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for each recorded backorder.
Fulfillment lists express orders before standard orders within one wave without changing its existing signature.
History analytics derives a backorders count from the event journal.
The API exposes the backorders of the current warehouse state.
The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.
The g6 probe returns one deterministic JSON object and its package script preserves byte-identical output across repeated invocations.
goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain - src/domain/orders.ts: export OrderPriority standard|express; make priority optional at call sites with standard as the default; reject invalid priorities with OrderError; export Backorder with orderId, skuId, positive integer missing; add backorders to WarehouseState; reserveOrder records shortages instead of throwing and leaves orders cancellable; export listBackorders.

Application - expose the new operations and emit a warehouse event for each recorded backorder. Fulfillment - order express before standard within one wave without changing the existing signature. Durability - derive a backorders count from the event journal. API - expose current-state backorders. Presentation - distinguish express and standard orders in rendered SVG. Probe - add study:g6-probe that emits one deterministic JSON object with no extra stdout. Preserve existing behavior and tests; add focused tests beside the covered code.
